description: The database tables the repository knows about, including aliases and tables that are really SQL statements.
row_meaning: One physical table object in the repository.

description: What each physical table stands for in the database: the SQL of a table of type 'select', or the database object's name for any other type.
row_meaning: One definition of one physical table for one database type.

description: The columns of the physical tables.
row_meaning: One column of one physical table.

description: The joins between physical tables. Two kinds share the table: a foreign key declared on a table, and a complex join between two tables with a condition of its own.
row_meaning: One foreign key of one physical table, or one complex join.

description: The keys declared on physical tables: each names the column or columns whose values identify a row of the table. A foreign key of another table points at one of these. Not in the first attempt's Knowledge Base (deliberate difference 28).
row_meaning: One key of one physical table.

description: The tables of the business models: the logical facts and dimensions that measures and attributes are defined on.
row_meaning: One logical table of one business model.

description: The columns of the logical tables, with their formulas exactly as written. This is where each measure and attribute is defined.
row_meaning: One column of one logical table.

description: The keys declared on logical tables: each names the logical column or columns whose values identify a row of the logical table. Not in the first attempt's Knowledge Base (deliberate difference 29).
row_meaning: One key of one logical table.

description: How each measure is aggregated: its default rule and any rule that replaces the default for particular dimensions.
row_meaning: One aggregation rule of one measure.

description: The table sources of the logical tables: each is one way a logical table is answered from physical tables, with its content filter, fragment and grain.
row_meaning: One table source of one logical table.

description: The column mappings of the table sources: which physical expression supplies each logical column through each source.
row_meaning: One logical column mapped through one table source.

description: The physical tables each logical table source is built on, as the source itself lists them. A source with more than one joins them; see lts_joins. Not in the first attempt's Knowledge Base (deliberate difference 34).
row_meaning: One physical table of one table source.

description: The joins each logical table source makes between its physical tables, with the join type. This is where an inner or outer join inside a source is recorded: it decides which rows a measure counts, and no formula shows it. Not in the first attempt's Knowledge Base (deliberate difference 34).
row_meaning: One join of one table source, as listed under one of the two tables it joins.

description: The joins between logical tables, with the join type (inner or outer) and how many rows each side may have. An inner join drops rows that have no partner, so it can change a number without changing any formula.
row_meaning: One join between two logical tables.

description: The logical dimensions: the drill structure behind each hierarchy, with flags for ragged, skip-level and parent-child hierarchies.
row_meaning: One logical dimension of one business model.

description: The levels of the logical dimensions, each with the column a drill follows.
row_meaning: One level of one logical dimension.

description: The keys declared on the levels of logical dimensions: the column or columns whose values identify a member of the level, with the flags that say which key is the level's primary key, which gives the order in time, and which a drill shows. Not in the first attempt's Knowledge Base (deliberate difference 30).
row_meaning: One key of one level of a logical dimension.

description: The subject areas: the groups of presentation tables a report author chooses from. A report names its subject area.
row_meaning: One subject area.

description: The tables of the subject areas, as a report author sees them (folders of columns).
row_meaning: One presentation table of one subject area.

description: The columns of the presentation tables, as a report author sees them, each tied to the logical column it shows.
row_meaning: One column of one presentation table.

description: The hierarchies a report author sees on a presentation table, each tied to its logical dimension.
row_meaning: One hierarchy of one presentation table.

description: The levels of the presentation hierarchies, in drill order.
row_meaning: One level of one presentation hierarchy.

description: The presentation columns shown at each level of a presentation hierarchy.
row_meaning: One presentation column shown at one level.

description: Where each presentation column comes from: the path from presentation column through logical column and table source to physical table and column. Repository lineage only; report columns are not in this table.
row_meaning: One path: one presentation column through one table source that maps its logical column.

description: The repository and session variables, with their default values. A formula or filter that uses a variable changes its result when the variable changes.
row_meaning: One variable.

description: The initialization blocks: the queries that fill variables when the server starts or a user signs in.
row_meaning: One initialization block.

description: The repository's security: which role holds which query privilege, which permission a privilege package has on which object, and the row filters on table sources. Three kinds of row share the table.
row_meaning: One query privilege of one role, one object one permission applies to, or one row filter.

description: The dashboards in the Web Catalog. A dashboard is a layout object that lists its pages.
row_meaning: One dashboard layout object.

description: The dashboard pages in the Web Catalog, each with the dashboard that lists it.
row_meaning: One dashboard page object.

description: What dashboards and pages hold: a dashboard's references to its pages, and a page's references to reports, dashboard prompts, scorecard views and folders, each with how the reference resolved.
row_meaning: One reference written in a dashboard or a dashboard page.

description: The reports in the Web Catalog. OBIEE calls a report an analysis, and the tables keep that word.
row_meaning: One report object.

description: The criteria blocks of reports. A criteria block is one query definition: a subject area, columns and filters. A report that combines queries has several.
row_meaning: One criteria block of one report.

description: The columns of reports, each with its formula exactly as written. This is where a calculation that exists only in a report is defined.
row_meaning: One column of one criteria block of a report.

description: The views inside reports: what each report is shown as (a table, a pivot table, a chart, a title, a layout that arranges other views).
row_meaning: One view inside one report.

description: Filters: every expression of the filters inside reports, every expression of the saved filters, and the dashboard prompts placed on dashboard pages. Read scope first.
row_meaning: One expression of a filter (scope 'analysis' or 'saved_filter'), or one dashboard prompt placed on a page (scope 'dashboard').

description: The prompts defined inside reports. Dashboard prompts are separate catalog objects, which are not read, so this table holds only the few prompts that sit inside a report.
row_meaning: One prompt inside one report.

description: The saved filters in the Web Catalog: filters kept as objects of their own, which reports refer to by path. The conditions of each are in analysis_filters.
row_meaning: One saved filter object.

description: Each report column followed towards the repository: the presentation column its formula names and, through repository lineage, the logical and physical column; or the reason there is no link. This is the only table that joins the Web Catalog to the repository.
row_meaning: One report column: exactly one row for every row of analysis_columns.

description: Known gaps: content that is in the source and is not carried by any Knowledge Base table. Nothing here is a failure.
row_meaning: One kind of content that was not read, for one object type, with how often it occurs.

description: Things that went wrong: content that should have been captured and was not. Empty when the run was clean.
row_meaning: One problem found during the run.

description: The work units of this Slice, in the order a document about it should be written. A skill takes one unit at a time and reads only that unit's packet.
row_meaning: One work unit: one packet file under packets/.

description: The rows a document about this Slice must cover: each must be cited as [kb:<row_id>] or listed in the document's 'Not described' section with a reason. check-doc reads this list; it is the completeness contract between slice and check-doc.
row_meaning: One row of a Slice table that a document must cover.

description: The FSD's items that need data, each with the columns the Operator confirmed for it, its decision notes, and the FSD's words and anchor. Only in a Slice cut for a tab. Built from the tab's fsd_items.csv, matches.csv and decisions.csv; the rows a to-be document cites for the tab's fields.
row_meaning: One item of the FSD (not the row naming the page the tab replaces).

description: The list of tables in this Knowledge Base and what each holds. Start here.
row_meaning: One table (one CSV file) of the Knowledge Base.

description: Every column of every table: what it means and which other table it points at.
row_meaning: One column of one table.

description: What produced this Slice, from which Knowledge Base and subject area, and the list of its tables.
row_meaning: One fact about the Slice, as a key and a value.
